findings.claim: The open command's session query (line 302) selects id, state, judging_body, quorum_required, quorum_observed, updated_at, created_at but omits version, so requireEtag (line 1393) computes the expected token as W/"undefined": every legitimate numeric ETag emitted by the previous session command (e.g. convene-extraordinary returns W/"<n>" via returning *) is rejected with 412 RAIT.VERSION_CONFLICT, while the constant string W/"undefined" bypasses the version confrontation entirely; open's UPDATE (line 374) also never increments version. The frozen suites cannot catch this because the only open sensors are the dispatch fixture and the composition E2E that asserts status !== 404 (rait-session-agenda-production.e2e.spec.ts:140), so prior high item 4 (ETag round-trip in the session service) is not fully closed.
findings.fix: Add version to the open select (or route open through lockSession, which already selects it), increment version in the open UPDATE like every other session mutation, and extend the real-DB structural sensor with a convene/open (or equivalent) sequence that proves the previous command's ETag is accepted by open's If-Match guard.

findings.claim: declare-batch-item-impediment passes the rait_batch_item row to recordMutation, but inf.rait_batch_item has no version column (backend/database/ddl/35-inf-rait-worklist.sql:314-335), so Number(data.version) is NaN and the response ETag falls back to W/"<id>:<updated_at>" (line 1310), a token requireExpectedVersion (line 121) can never accept; the batch version is meanwhile incremented without RETURNING (line 953), so the post-transaction parent version is not surfaced anywhere in the response. A client following the contracted envelope cannot chain the next accept/impediment on the same batch, which is the exact defect class of prior high item 4, and CTG-0002 §2 explicitly forbids using a child ETag without version.
findings.fix: Have declare-batch-item-impediment return the batch's post-transaction row (RETURNING * on the batch version bump) to recordMutation, or otherwise emit the parent batch's numeric version as the success ETag, and cover the impediment→accept ETag chain in the frozen real-DB sensor.

findings.claim: reassign requires the If-Match header to be present (validateEnvelope line 105) but never calls requireExpectedVersion, so the version is never confronted (any token is accepted), and its response ETag is the new rait_assignment row's fallback token because inf.rait_assignment has no version column; draw is additionally absent from the If-Match-required command list (line 104-110) although it mutates an existing LOTE_ABERTO batch, so the §2 envelope (428/412 on the versioned parent aggregate) is not enforced for these two commands. Concurrency remains bounded by FOR UPDATE locks, the active-assignment guard and the LOTE_ABERTO state guard, so this is envelope discipline, not a lost-write hole.
findings.fix: Confront the aggregate version under lock in reassign (batch or a versioned assignment representation added by blueprint) and add draw to the If-Match-required set, emitting the parent's post-transaction numeric version in both responses.

findings.claim: draw performs no requirePoolBinding check: unlike create-schedule, publish-schedule, create-batch and approve-batch, the acting secretary's active membership in the batch's pool is not revalidated in the database, so authorization rests on the exact-role policy plus tenant RLS alone. This is the same acknowledged class as the prior low on the session presidency commands (open/close-agenda/adjourn/convene without a DB chair binding), now also present in the newly implemented draw.
findings.fix: Call requirePoolBinding(tx, context, batch.pool_id) in draw before generating the seed, mirroring the sibling worklist commands, with a negative sensor for an unbound secretary.

findings.claim: publish arms T-R2 through the deadline engine in the same transaction only for JARI proclaimed items, and the catalog/store support it (timer-catalog T-R2, rait_deadline check constraint includes T-R2), but no frozen sensor exercises publish with an actual proclaimed item: the structural E2E publishes a session with zero agenda items, so the T-R2 arm path (and the per-item publishSessionDecision loop) is verified by code reading only, not by executed evidence. The T-VOTO half of prior high item 2 is fully proven in the real-DB sensor.
findings.fix: Extend the frozen real-DB structural sensor with a proclaimed JARI agenda item so publish provably transitions the case JULGADO_SESSAO→COMUNICADO and inserts the T-R2 row in inf.rait_deadline in the same transaction.

findings.claim: draw forwards the client's opaque Idempotency-Key to the trust provider in prepareBatchMinutesManifest, and createMinutes does the same for prepareSessionMinutesManifest (rait-session-command.service.ts:937), while CTG-0002-TECHNICAL-CLOSURE-CONTRACT.md §2 requires the provider key to be server-derived from kind, tenant, aggregate and snapshotHash. The manifest itself remains server-owned, exactly validated and unique per batch/minutes, so this is a bounded contract deviation, not a trust bypass.
findings.fix: Derive the provider idempotency key server-side (e.g. sha256 of documentKind:tenantId:aggregateId:snapshotHash) inside the adapter or at the call sites, keeping the client key only for the HTTP command's own idempotency record.

notes: Prior high 1 (minutes immutability) is CLOSED: BP-INF-RAIT-SESSION-001 v1.2.2 declares immutableColumns [id, tenant_id, session_id, content, generated_at, document_hash], tools/blueprints/generate.mjs emits the column-scoped trigger, ddl/36 line 435 matches the generated output, and the real-DB structural sensor proves the positive sign→publish lifecycle (signed_at/published_at persisted, ETags W/"1"→W/"2"→W/"3") while a content UPDATE still fails with 42501. Snapshot, manifest, required-signer, receipt and vote tables remain fully immutable.

Prior high 2 (accept transition + T-VOTO) is CLOSED for the accept half: RaitCaseTransitionPort now exposes acceptBatchItem, accept-batch-item calls it in the same transaction (DISTRIBUIDO→EM_INSTRUCAO with case event and outbox) and arms T-VOTO via the deadline engine into inf.rait_deadline, proven 2/2 against the real DDL. The publish/T-R2 half is implemented in the same transaction and the engine/catalog/DDL support it, but it lacks executed sensor coverage with a proclaimed item (low finding).

Prior high 3 (server-owned draw) is CLOSED: draw generates a server seed (randomBytes 32), orders eligible members by seeded hash with member-id tie-break, persists per-item member/claim_due_on (T-CLAIM via the deadline engine, 2 business days), inserts active assignments, freezes the canonical snapshot with SHA-256 into immutable inf.rait_batch_draw_snapshot, prepares and persists the immutable batch minutes manifest with the chair as expected signer, and flips LOTE_SORTEADO — all in the command transaction, proven in the real-DB sensor. approve-batch verifies snapshot hash, manifest completeness, provider-recovered manifest equality and the fail-closed receipt before homologation; accept requires homologated_at.

Prior high 4 (ETag round-trip) is PARTIALLY CLOSED: requireExpectedVersion/requireEtag now parse numeric W/"<version>" tokens and recordMutation emits them for all versioned aggregates; the draw→accept chain (W/"2"→W/"3") and sign→publish chain are proven against the real DDL. Residuals: session open confronts If-Match against an unselected version (always W/"undefined", high), and declare-batch-item-impediment emits a non-parseable child fallback token (high); reassign never confronts the version and draw omits If-Match entirely (low).

No regression of the eight original items was found: exactly 20 nominal POST handlers remain (8 worklist, 12 session), oral-arguments stays suppressed, DDL 35/36 changes are additive with guarded constraints and tenant-first composite FKs, the unique indexes precede the composite FKs they support, RLS/tenant triggers and role_app_backend grants are intact, the DocumentTrustHttpAdapter remains fail-closed with distinct batch/session capabilities, the OWNER signer decision (chair + item rapporteurs, absence frozen in the snapshot, secretary excluded) is implemented in createMinutes/required_signer, and run-backend-ci.mjs remains an honest fail-closed sequence ending in the destructive upgrade rehearsal.

The six acknowledged lows from the first review persist unchanged and remain non-structural under the OWNER good-enough direction: /commands/sign route drift, hardcoded audit role literals ('rait-coordinator'/'rait-secretary'), single-event recordMutation omitting rait.assignment.changed on impediment/reassign, vote without a read_at guard and presidency commands without DB chair binding, inline T-CONV business-day computation and current_date/clock_timestamp guard decisions, and the evidence-traceability gap on the final pnpm check attribution. None was promoted; none was silently claimed as fixed.

Closure evidence is honest: TASK-0078 preserves the FAIL verdict and candidate hash, TASK-0079 records the bounded corrective slice with backend:test:ci exit 0 (E2E 125/125, upgrade 18/18), pnpm check exit 0 and the structural sensor 2/2, and the code I read is consistent with those claims. The FINAL-CANDIDATE statement that 'ETag numérico é emitido e aceito em round-trip' is overbroad only with respect to the two item-4 residuals above.

Verdict rationale: REVIEW, not FAIL — three of the four prior highs are closed with executed real-DB proof and no security, integrity, authorization or evidence fabrication was found, but correction 4 is incomplete in two bounded, precisely locatable spots (session open's If-Match guard and the impediment response ETag), so PASS is barred until a small corrective slice with sensors closes them.
